subject: science
title: Animal Groups
about: Sorting animals into six groups by what covers their body, how many legs they have and where they start life: mammals (fur, milk), birds (feathers, eggs, two legs), fish (fins, gills), reptiles (dry scales), amphibians (frogs: water, then land) and insects (six legs). Animal groups are not named in NC's 2023 Grade 1 standards; this bridge deck sits under LS.1.1.2 because each group's body parts fit the place that meets its needs.
tip: Play 'which group?' with the animals on a walk or in a picture book: fur or feathers, how many legs, wet skin or dry scales.

cards.q: A dog has fur and drank its mother's milk as a puppy. What group is a dog in?
cards.note: Mammals have fur or hair and feed their babies milk.

cards.q: You have hair and drank milk as a baby. Which animal group are people in?
cards.note: People are mammals, just like dogs, cats and cows.
Only birds have feathers. Feathers keep them warm and help them fly.

cards.q: How many legs does a bird have?
cards.note: Two legs and two wings. A bird also has a beak instead of teeth.

cards.q: A hen lays eggs with hard shells. What group does a hen belong to?
cards.note: Baby birds hatch out of eggs. Most mammals are born, not hatched.

cards.q: Which animal group breathes with gills and swims with fins?
cards.note: Most fish are covered in slippery scales.

cards.q: A snake has dry, scaly skin. Is a snake a reptile, a bird or a fish?
cards.note: Reptiles have dry scales. Snakes, lizards, turtles and alligators are reptiles.

cards.q: A lizard with dry scales warms up on a sunny rock. What kind of animal is a lizard?
cards.note: Reptiles sit in the sun to warm their bodies.

cards.q: A frog starts life in the water and then lives on land. What group is a frog in?
cards.note: Say am-FIB-ee-uns. Amphibians have thin, damp skin with no scales. Toads and salamanders are amphibians too.

cards.q: A frog has wet skin. A lizard has dry scales. A dog has fur. Which one is the reptile?
cards.note: Wet skin means amphibian. Dry scales mean reptile.

cards.q: How many legs does an insect have?
cards.note: A spider has eight legs, so a spider is not an insect.

cards.q: A ladybug has six legs. Which group does a ladybug belong to?
cards.note: Insects have six legs and three body parts. Most have wings too.
Feathers, a beak and two legs. An eagle is a bird.
A shark has gills and fins, so it is a fish. A whale is not a fish.

cards.q: A whale breathes air and feeds its baby milk. Is a whale a mammal or a fish?
cards.note: A whale lives in the sea, but it comes up to breathe air through a blowhole.
An alligator has dry, scaly skin. Alligators live in the warm rivers near North Carolina's coast.
Count the legs. A bee has six. A spider has eight and a worm has none.

cards.q: A penguin has feathers and lays eggs, but it swims instead of flying. What group is a penguin in?
cards.note: A penguin uses its wings to swim instead of fly. It is still a bird.
